title: Single-dip CPV candidates among old TESS M dwarfs show eclipsing-binary signatures; without them a pre-registered test of three TESS samples finds 1 CPV where contraction predicts 6.3 (p = 0.026)
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, fast-rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. A frozen contraction-only (x-only) model predicts CPVs among old main-sequence M dwarfs at the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x of young hosts. Earlier TESS 2-minute and 200-s samples gave 3 CPVs for about 5.7 predicted, and the old candidates had one narrow dip. We built a third, disjoint sample from 10-min TESS-SPOC full-frame light curves of 19,978 M dwarfs within 100 pc and pre-registered the test. TESS pixels put the period on another star for 15 of 26 old stars with P < 0.3 d. Among 69 old rapid rotators in the model x range (38 effective on-target stars) the model predicts 0.59 CPVs and we observe 1, a single-dip star. All three samples give 4 for 6.33 (p = 0.28). In all three on-target single-dip candidates (8 sectors) the dip falls on a minimum of the second harmonic of the light curve, as eclipses at conjunction in a tidally locked binary do (null p = 0.005-0.046 per star; young CPV dips do not align). The stars lie 0.6-1.5 mag below the main sequence, trapezoid dips fit better than Gaussians, and the ellipsoidal amplitudes need a massive companion that is faint in TESS, probably a cool white dwarf. With the pre-registered two-dip rule, 1 CPV is seen for 6.33 predicted (p = 0.026). Thus no old M dwarf yet shows young-CPV morphology, which favours an age factor beyond contraction. Limitations: the new sample alone predicts only 0.59 CPVs, the binary classification has no spectra, and one agent made the labels.
